newsitem.title: USA: House panel votes to overturn Mexico drug decision.
newsitem.headline: House panel votes to overturn Mexico drug decision.

text.p: A U.S. House of Representatives committee voted on Thursday to disapprove President Bill Clinton's certification that Mexico is cooperating fully with the United States in the anti-narcotics war.
The International Relations committee also voted to waive sanctions against Mexico that would normally accompany the decertification of its drug efforts.
The resolution, approved by a 27-5 vote, was sent to the full House for action.
Similar legislation has been introduced in the Senate.

The administration opposes decertification of Mexico, but a State Department official acknowledged that the waiver approved by the committee was broader and more useful to Clinton than the one he is able to invoke on the grounds of national interests in current law.
Assistant Secretary of State Jeffrey Davidow told the committee that the resolution was "counterproductive" and said of Mexico's anti-drug operations: "The trend is clearly positive."
